Decorative image elements
+ +

Decorative image elements are images which don't have any accessibility information
body:
wcag has a definition of "[pure decoration](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#dfn-pure-decoration)" - if might that be referenced?

since 4.8.4.4.7 "Ancillary images" and 4.8.4.4.8 "A purely decorative image that doesn't add any information" already exist in the spec, should this reference those existing sections / those sections reference this?  

in the context of a customized select element, i believe people will often reach for `img`, `svg` or some generic / generic-ish element to render a font icon or emoji and set that to aria-hidden=true.  But if defining this as a specific set of elements, then arguably that moves the scope beyond just what's needed in a select, and probably needs to consider things like `picture` containing an img with alt="", or an object or canvas element used to render a graphic, but similar to svg, set to aria-hidden=true.  


but maybe instead of adding this category of elements (and i'm sure other people will have thoughts on this), the content model for select could just specifically state that an img element with alt="" or svg with aria-hidden=true is allowed (arguably a picture element if it similarly contains an img alt="").  And maybe detached from this specific feature, a decorative images category could be created?

looking through other element content models, there is precedent for allowing specific elements rather than categories, even with stipulations the elements have (or don't have) certain attributes.

If the element has a label attribute but no value attribute: Text.
If the element has no label attribute and is not a - child of a datalist element: Text that is not - inter-element whitespace.
-
If the element has no label attribute and is a child - of a datalist element: Text.
+ child of a datalist element: Zero or more option element + inner content elements.
body: I pushed a change to make options allowed as descendants of datalist elements, and if they are a descendant of a datalist element, only text is allowed in their content. I believe this should address all concerns in this thread.
